tema: Quantifies, by meta-analysis, circulating inflammatory proteins in CFS patients versus controls.
diseno: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 42 studies with patients diagnosed with CFS and unaffected controls; quality assessment based on Newcastle-Ottawa, sensitivity analysis and publication bias analysis.
hallazgos: CFS patients had elevated TNF (ES = 0.274), IL-2 (ES = 0.203), IL-4 (ES = 0.373), TGF-β (ES = 0.967) and CRP (ES = 0.622); 12 proteins did not differ between groups.
conclusion: The data partly support an inflammatory component in CFS, although the inconsistency of results limits the conclusions.
triangulacion: The abstract is (truncated) opening text and the 'conclusions' are quality appendices, forest and funnel plots; the latter suggest possible publication bias for TNFα and IL-2 (Egger test), a nuance that reinforces caution. The keywords match the markers highlighted.

tema: Models post-exertional malaise by comparing CSF miRNAs from subjects with and without prior exercise and infers the affected brain pathways.
diseno: Comparison of CSF miRNAs between subjects at rest (n = 45) and after submaximal exercise (n = 15) before lumbar puncture; computational analysis with DIANA MiRpath v3.0, TarBase, Cytoscape and Ingenuity. Registrations NCT01291758 and NCT00810225.
hallazgos: miR-608, miR-328, miR-200a-5p, miR-93-3p and miR-92a-3p were higher at rest than after exercise. DIANA found 33 targets that could rise after exercise (TGFBR1, IGFR1, CDC42), with a predominance of adhesion pathways; Ingenuity selected seven targets (GNAQ, ADCY3, RAP1B, PIK3R3) expressed in choroid plexus, neurons and microglia.
conclusion: The reduction of this combination of CSF miRNAs after exercise suggests upregulation of phosphoinositol pathways and altered adhesion during the PEM of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources agree (conclusions taken from the abstract) on PEM, physical activity and specific miRNAs; the keywords omit the CSF and the inferred pathways, and the conclusion is inferential, based on computational prediction.

tema: Uses invasive CPET (iCPET) and skin biopsies to study the pathophysiology of exercise intolerance in ME/CFS and its relationship to small fibre neuropathy (SFN).
diseno: Analysis of 1516 iCPETs; 160 ME/CFS patients with skin biopsy (PGP9.5) are compared with 36 controls; tertiles of the Qc/VO2 slope.
hallazgos: Detailed results are not stated in the available opening text. The discussion describes physiological subtypes of low and high pulmonary flow, the latter associated with altered peripheral oxygen extraction, and a first association between small fibre pathology and ME/CFS.
conclusion: The hypothesis is generated that peripheral vascular dysregulation causes exercise intolerance in ME/CFS; broader assessment of the contribution of SFN is recommended.
triangulacion: The abstract is opening text truncated before the results, so the discussion provides the findings. The keywords (SFN, POTS, fibromyalgia, biopsy) are consistent with both sources.

tema: Gathers perspectives of people with ME/CFS on research, clinical interactions and case definition.
diseno: Analysis of contributions from people with ME/CFS (DePaul); sample size and method not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Participants are frustrated with research and clinical care but motivated to contribute; a case definition without PEM as a core symptom would hardly be accepted; they propose that the case definition used in each study be reported.
conclusion: People with ME/CFS have first-hand knowledge and an important role in the consensus on case definition.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the abstract is opening text (citation and acknowledgements); the substantive information comes only from the conclusions, consistent with the title.

tema: Reviews metabolomic findings in ME/CFS patients and in animal models with a view to developing diagnostic biomarkers.
diseno: Narrative review of metabolomic studies in humans and animal models of fatigue. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Common metabolic fluctuations are observed between animal models and patients; d-ROMs, exosomes and microRNAs, monocyte count, lipoprotein profiles, cytokines and PET-detected neuroinflammation are cited as informative markers.
conclusion: Biomarker research is still evolving; the authors are confident of establishing objective biomarkers by integrating metabolomic markers with high-precision in vivo biomarkers.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the metabolomic and diagnostic focus. The conclusions broaden to inflammation and neuroinflammation, beyond the metabolic scope of the abstract.

tema: Identifies ME/CFS subtypes by integrating DNA methylation profiles in immune cells with health scores.
diseno: Study in 70 women with ME/CFS; integration of immune cell methylomes with RAND-36 and the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire through similarity network fusion.
hallazgos: Four subtypes were identified associated with methylation differences at 1939 CpG sites, three RAND-36 categories (physical function, social function and physical limitations) and five DePaul measures; methylation of immune response genes and differences in physical function and PEM differentiated the subtypes.
conclusion: The subtypes are associated with specific methylation and symptom differences, supporting the relevance of immune and metabolic differences, and the integrative strategy could contribute to a new nosology, diagnostic criteria and targeted therapies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent on methylation, subtypes and physical function; the conclusions broaden the projection toward personalized medicine and its application to other complex diseases.

tema: Presents a model of interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy adapted to patients with post-viral syndromes and ME/CFS with PEM.
diseno: Literature summary, description of clinical features and presentation of a model project in a day hospital; no sample.
hallazgos: The usual multimodal, group and activating programmes do not sufficiently take into account stress intolerance with PEM, so physical and psychological overload must be avoided.
conclusion: A multimodal day-hospital pain treatment adjusted to individual capacity is proposed, minimizing the risk of exertion-induced worsening.
triangulacion: No conclusions are available; keywords (multimodal pain, personalized treatment, physical overload) and abstract are consistent with each other.

tema: Investigates whether graded and intermittent exercise improves CD8+ lymphocyte activation and NK cell degranulation markers in CFS/ME compared with usual care.
diseno: Randomized trial with 24 CFS patients (50.2 ± 10 years) assigned to graded exercise, intermittent exercise or usual care for 12 weeks, plus 18 sedentary controls for immunological comparisons; cytometry (CD8+CD38+, LAMP-1/LAMP-2) and aerobic capacity.
hallazgos: After the intervention, the percentage of NK cells with LAMP-1/-2 was higher with intermittent exercise versus usual care and with graded exercise versus usual care and controls; both exercises increased pre-post expression and improved aerobic capacity. There were no significant changes in CD8+CD38+.
conclusion: Both modalities increased NK activation and degranulation markers and exercise capacity without worsening symptoms, and could reduce CD8+CD38+; larger and longer trials are warranted.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; abstract and conclusions assert a possible reduction of CD8+CD38+ despite there being no significant pre-post changes, a nuance to consider. The keywords focus on NK and exercise.

tema: Determines the frequency and severity of fatigue and CFS in patients with episodic and chronic migraine and their relationship to other comorbidities.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 60 migraine patients (30 episodic and 30 chronic) at a tertiary centre in New Delhi; HIT-6, FSS, Chalder scale, CDC CFS criteria, ACR fibromyalgia criteria, depression, anxiety (GAD-7) and sleepiness (ESS) scales.
hallazgos: About 23.33% of chronic migraine patients met CFS criteria. Fatigue correlated with migraine severity, frequency, duration and chronicity, and with depression, anxiety and excessive daytime sleepiness.
conclusion: Fatigue, CFS and related comorbidities are more frequent and severe in chronic than in episodic migraine; a comprehensive approach that includes fatigue management and psychosocial support, and broader population studies, are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The abstract's results are truncated; the PDF conclusions add behavioural therapy and the explicit mention of fibromyalgia and depression as the most frequent comorbidities in migraineurs with fatigue.

tema: Directly evaluates connectivity within and from the brainstem in ME/CFS using fMRI.
diseno: Resting-state and task fMRI in 45 patients (Fukuda criteria) and 27 controls; ROIs of the reticular activating system (rostral medulla, cuneiform nucleus), dorsal raphe, hippocampal subiculum and thalamic intralaminar nucleus.
hallazgos: In ME/CFS, connections between the medulla and midbrain nuclei were missing, while hippocampal connections were strengthened. During the task, medulla-cuneiform and brainstem-hippocampus/thalamus connectivity deficits were detected, and lower connectivity was associated with greater severity.
conclusion: Reticular activating system connectivity is altered and could explain many symptoms; the hippocampus would have a compensatory role.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent (brainstem, RAS, hippocampus); the abstract develops further the mechanistic link with attention, sleep and muscle tone.

tema: Studies whether intracranial compliance and cerebral perfusion are associated with orthostatic intolerance symptoms in CFS.
diseno: Study with 40 CFS patients and 10 matched controls; phase-contrast flow MRI (arterial, venous and CSF flow), arterial spin labelling perfusion (FAIR) and Autonomic Symptom Profile.
hallazgos: Patients reported more OI. In them, greater OI severity was associated with lower intracranial compliance (r=-0.346) and higher resting perfusion (r=0.337); there were no differences between groups in compliance or perfusion.
conclusion: Low intracranial compliance and high resting perfusion are associated with more severe OI, perhaps because of poorer cerebral autoregulation, although it may not be specific to CFS; replication is required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the discussion is more cautious, raises compliance as a possible risk factor and suggests replicating with transcranial Doppler. The conclusions section includes noise from author contributions.

tema: Feasibility study examining antibody reactivity against the gut microbiome in severe ME/CFS to test the hypothesis of intestinal permeability and microbial translocation.
diseno: Pilot study with 5 pairs of severe ME/CFS patients and healthy controls from the same household; measurement of secretory IgA and serum IgG and development of IgG-Seq (flow cytometry plus metagenomics).
hallazgos: Immune dysfunction was observed in severe ME/CFS, with lower capacity and reactivity of serum IgG against faecal microbes, regardless of their origin.
conclusion: It is the first study of serum IgG reactivity to the gut microbiome in ME/CFS; it suggests an altered IgG response and lays the groundwork for investigating the leaky gut hypothesis in larger cohorts.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The keywords (permeability, translocation) reflect the starting hypothesis more than the findings, which show lower reactivity and do not directly confirm translocation.

tema: Doctoral thesis (University of Edinburgh, 2022) investigating the genetic and immunological aetiology of ME/CFS.
diseno: Thesis with several genetic studies, including a GWAS in UK Biobank with new composite phenotypes; other details of population and methods are not stated in the opening text.
hallazgos: The GWAS was the most useful tool and found the only statistically significant association of all the studies, in relation to the PDE10A gene (variant rs76346913), considered together with SLC25A15 one of the strongest genetic signals detected for ME/CFS.
conclusion: GWAS remains the best starting point; a replication GWAS is proposed to confirm rs76346913 as a risk allele and studies with more participants and precise phenotyping.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the abstract is the opening text of the thesis (cover and copyright notices), so the substantive information comes only from the PDF conclusions; triangulation is not possible.

tema: Characterizes the gut DNA virome in severe ME/CFS and predicts virus-host interactions associated with the disease.
diseno: Study in a small cohort of severe ME/CFS patients and healthy controls from the same household; sequencing of virus-like particles (VLP) and whole metagenomes from the same faecal sample, with in silico prediction of interactions. Exact size not stated.
hallazgos: A core virome of tailed phages (Caudoviricetes) and greater diversity of DNA viruses were identified. There were no significant differences in viral or bacterial abundance or diversity between groups, but interactions between the genus Anaerotruncus and viruses unique to ME/CFS were predicted.
conclusion: The study provides a framework and rationale for investigating in larger cohorts the interactions between gut virome and bacteriome associated with ME/CFS.
triangulacion: General coherence among the three sources. The conclusions add the nuance, absent from the abstract, that there were no significant differences in abundance or diversity between groups.

tema: Investigates the factors associated with a clinically important improvement in the SF-36-PFS in young people with ME/CFS at a specialist NHS service.
diseno: Prospective observational cohort: 193 patients aged 8-17; follow-up data in 124 (6 months) and 121 (12 months); logistic regression.
hallazgos: 40% reached the MCID at 6 months and 54% at 12 months; worse baseline physical function was associated with the MCID at 6 months, and pain and physical function at 12 months; no other baseline factor was associated.
conclusion: There are no robust baseline predictors; the SF-36-PFS may not be the most suitable measure in young people and a multi-domain measure is needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions emphasize more the inadequacy of the SF-36-PFS and the need for an adjusted MCID.

tema: Explores the experiences of adult women with ME/CFS in England regarding the factors that affect their occupational participation.
diseno: Qualitative study with semi-structured interviews with 9 women (purposive sampling); analysis with thematic networks.
hallazgos: Four organizing themes (factors of impairment, person, environment and society) and two global themes: invisibility and diagnostic stigma.
conclusion: Many participation problems are secondary to environmental factors and preventable; the lack of empathy owing to disbelief can cause harm and is neither ethical nor professional.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add ethical and disability-rights implications and acknowledge the possible variation of diagnostic criteria.

tema: Book on the history of invisible illnesses, from hysteria to long COVID.
diseno: Historical-anthropological essay book; no methodology stated.
hallazgos: Draws parallels between neurasthenia and the 19th-century rest cure and current conditions lacking verifiability, which remain in a liminal state of legitimacy.
conclusion: Proposes elevating the experience of complex patients as a legitimate source of knowledge and sees long COVID as a window for a healthcare revolution.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the abstract is editorial text with no content; the conclusions text seems to be the introduction of the book, consistent with the title.

tema: Opinion article by a neurologist on the dismissive use of 'it's all in your head' in the face of medically unexplained symptoms.
diseno: Opinion article (JAMA Neurology); no empirical data.
hallazgos: Inadequate management of medically unexplained symptoms (functional neurological disorder, CFS, fibromyalgia) is a silent epidemic that erodes the doctor-patient relationship; neuroimaging shows changes in brain networks.
conclusion: More research and a cultural change are required to eliminate negative connotations, with more consultation time, transparent diagnostic explanation, interdisciplinary referral and training.
triangulacion: Keywords (somatic symptom disorder, conversion) and texts agree; the abstract is opening text of the article. The framing is functional/psychosomatic, with CFS mentioned only as an example.

tema: Evaluates whether the protein cargo of extracellular vesicles responds abnormally to maximal exercise in women with ME/CFS and its relationship to PEM.
diseno: Case-control study: 18 women with ME/CFS and 17 sedentary controls matched for age and BMI; EVs isolated from plasma before, 15 min and 24 h after maximal CPET; nanoparticle tracking analysis and TMT proteomics.
hallazgos: Exercise altered the EV proteome differently in patients and controls, and post-exercise changes correlated strongly with symptom severity. The differential proteins were involved in coagulation, muscle contraction, cytoskeleton, immune system and brain signalling.
conclusion: Dysregulated EV release and their aberrant cargo after exercise could be involved in PEM in women with ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent on EVs, exercise intolerance and PEM; the conclusions (with noise from author contributions) formulate the role in PEM hypothetically.

tema: Examines whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for developing ME/CFS after infectious mononucleosis.
diseno: Substudy of a prospective cohort of university students followed after mononucleosis: 53 with ME/CFS at six months and 66 recovered controls with the modified Beighton score, performed by a single examiner blind to diagnosis.
hallazgos: There were no statistically significant differences in the Beighton score between ME/CFS and recovered individuals. Women had significantly higher scores than men.
conclusion: No relationship was found between joint hypermobility and the development of ME/CFS after infectious mononucleosis.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent with a negative result. The discussion qualifies that the Beighton score alone does not rule out hypermobility (other connective tissue parameters were not measured); the keywords do not mention joint flexibility, the central focus of the study.

tema: Examines muscle acid handling after exercise in CFS/ME and its relationship to autonomic dysfunction.
diseno: Observational study at a regional fatigue service: 16 CFS patients and 8 matched controls; phosphorus magnetic resonance spectroscopy during plantar flexion at 35% of maximal contraction and resting heart rate variability.
hallazgos: Patients showed suppression of proton efflux immediately after exercise (1.1 vs. 3.6 mmol/L/min) and at maximum (2.7 vs. 3.8), and a prolonged time to maximum efflux (25.6 vs. 3.8 s). The normal correlations of efflux with minimum pH and with heart rate variability were lost.
conclusion: CFS/ME patients show abnormalities in intramuscular pH recovery after exercise, related to autonomic dysfunction; it is a potentially modifiable biological abnormality.
triangulacion: Full coherence: the conclusions come from the structured abstract itself and the keywords capture the same axes (proton efflux, autonomic dysfunction, spectroscopy).

tema: Compares kynurenine pathway metabolites and ratios between CFS, fibromyalgia (FM) and healthy controls, and their relationship to symptoms.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in women aged 18-60: 49 with CFS, 57 with FM and 54 controls; plasma analysis of tryptophan and kynurenine metabolites, adjusted for age, BMI, anxiety and depression.
hallazgos: Quinolinic acid differed between CFS and FM and was related to BMI. The neuroprotective KA/QA ratio was lower in CFS than in controls; in FM, KA/HK and KAT II activity were lower, associated with more pain. Anxiety and depression were not associated with the metabolites.
conclusion: Kynurenine metabolism is associated with CFS and FM and with fatigue and pain; its metabolites could be indicators and targets, although with caution because of the complexity of the symptoms.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add recommendations (weight reduction, smoking cessation) not directly derived from the abstract and a tone of caution.

tema: Proposes a model that links long COVID, POTS and ME/CFS through the circumventricular organs, homocysteine and MTHFR polymorphisms.
diseno: Hypothesis article (non-peer-reviewed preprint) based on a literature review; no own data.
hallazgos: Suggests that the circumventricular organs, lacking a blood-brain barrier, allow elevated homocysteine from MTHFR variants (677TT) to act on autonomic and neuroendocrine nuclei. Links a microbiome poor in butyrate and GABA, EBV and VZV reactivation through loss of T surveillance, bradykinin, oestrogens, oxidative stress and mitochondrial exhaustion.
conclusion: Long COVID would reveal an undiagnosed MTHFR 677TT present in 30-40% of the population, predominant among those with long COVID and POTS; POTS would represent the intersection between long COVID and ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on the BBB, circumventricular organs and MTHFR. There is a discrepancy in figures on the prevalence of the polymorphism (more than 50% in the abstract versus 30-40% in the conclusions); the text is a non-peer-reviewed preprint.

tema: Describes the immunological profile of adolescents with EBV infectious mononucleosis and its relationship to the development of chronic fatigue.
diseno: Substudy of the CEBA prospective cohort (200 adolescents with mononucleosis); samples within 6 weeks of onset and at 6 months; PBMC culture and stimulation (n = 68) and plasma inflammatory markers (n = 200); chronic fatigue defined with the Chalder questionnaire (CF+ n = 32 and n = 91 in the in vitro and plasma cohorts).
hallazgos: There was broad PBMC activation at baseline with high RANTES in the CF+ group, and a plasma inflammatory response with elevated T markers. At 6 months, RANTES remained elevated in CF+, the β-adrenergic response was altered and CRP remained elevated while other markers declined.
conclusion: Patients who develop chronic fatigue after mononucleosis show T activation and chronic low-grade inflammation at baseline and at 6 months; RANTES discriminates early between patients with and without fatigue.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (EBV, low-grade inflammation, T activation, RANTES). There is a nuance on the β-adrenergic response: the abstract describes it as increased and the PDF conclusions as attenuated.

tema: Editorial of a Biomedicines special issue on mechanisms, sequelae and treatment of post-COVID syndrome.
diseno: Editorial presenting 14 articles grouped into post-COVID treatment, neonatal impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection, risk factors for severe COVID-19, post-COVID pain phenotyping and others.
hallazgos: Notes that more than 100 persistent symptoms have been attributed to SARS-CoV-2. The conclusions text describes an imbalance of CD4, CD8 and NK lymphocytes and of immune checkpoints in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and post-COVID.
conclusion: The special issue addresses gaps on the identification, evolution, mechanisms and treatment of post-COVID syndrome; the conclusions fragment confirms immunological similarities between both pulmonary fibroses.
triangulacion: There is a discrepancy: keywords and abstract correspond to the editorial, whereas the PDF conclusions appear to come from a specific article on pulmonary fibrosis, not from the editorial. ME/CFS is not mentioned in any source.
